_note: WORLD SCALE: movementDrainPerMileBase was multiplied by 5 on 2026-09-30 to stay coupled to the route table's /5 world rescale. It was 0.06 from iteration 96, which reconciled battery range against route length so no shipped route was an unreachable destination; that reconciliation is UNCHANGED by this edit (worst build still manages ~1.09x the longest route) because drain and distance moved together. ALL RECONSTRUCTION. Tick = 1/60s. 1 mile = 1609.344 m. Battery 0-99. battery.movementDrainPerMileBase is NOT a free balance knob: it is RECONCILED against cities.json's route lengths, because the road has no charging stops and no way to abandon a car, so a route longer than the battery range is not a slow drive, it is an UNREACHABLE destination. It was 0.9, which the two scales multiply by (1 + 1.4 * weight/power) * (1 + 0.6 * speedFraction) into an effective 1.84-5.67 per mile at full speed - 17 to 54 miles of range against routes of 40-240 miles (mean 125). Fourteen of twenty-six routes could not be completed on one charge, INCLUDING the capture rig's own subcompact-on-small-plant, which has 28.6 miles against ny-albany's 150 and stranded at 19% of the way. The road screen mounts no menu and no actions, and abandonVehicle - which @/sim/road exports and documents as the SPEC's on-foot escape - is never called by @/app, so there was no recovery of any kind: a player who ran the battery down was stuck, with a HUD reporting 0% and nothing to press. 0.06 puts the WORST build (heaviest body on the weakest plant, a 6.304x multiplier) at 262 miles and the BEST (lightest on strongest, 2.048x) at 805, clearing the longest route with margin. The reduction is UNIFORM, so the vehicle-quality gradient is preserved exactly - a badly built car still has about a third of a good car's range, it just finishes the journey, and the battery becomes an economy across several cities rather than a countdown to being stuck. Re-derive rather than nudge: the constraint is (full / (base * worstMultiplier)) >= max(cities.json lengthMiles), and tests/unit/driving.test.ts asserts it from the real rulesets so the two cannot drift apart again silently.

city._note: Driving the plaza, not the highway: a walled city is tens of meters across, so this is its own value rather than the car's road top speed. Three times pedestrian.speedMps, roughly 15mph, which crosses the widest generated plaza in a couple of seconds without outrunning the interaction radius (one frame at the 0.25s dt clamp covers 1.65m against a 3.0m trigger circle, so a doorway can never be tunneled through).
